title: Sources: Haney, Paro agree to welterweight title unification

Email address Email address Continue with email or Continue with Google Continue with Apple EN Help Featured News Sources: Haney, Paro agree to welterweight title unification 0 0 Link copied! 3 days ago 0 0 Link copied! 3 days ago Nate Pardo-Marrero 3 days ago 1 min read Devin Haney and Liam Paro have agreed to a welterweight title unification bout. The Ring’s Mike Coppinger said on Thursday's episode of "Inside The Ring" that the two have reached a deal and the bout is expected to take place in the U.S. before the end of the year. Haney (33-0, 15 KOs) holds the WBO title, and Paro is the IBF champion. Haney, The Ring’s No. 1 welterweight and eighth pound-for-pound, hasn’t fought since beating Brian Norman by unanimous decision to become the WBO welterweight champion on November 22. The 27-year-old from Oakland became a three-division champion with the dominant decision victory over Norman (29-1, 23 KOs). Haney had been in discussions to face The Ring and WBO 140-pound champion Shakur Stevenson. Those talks fell through, with the weight and a rehydration clause being among the issues that prevented it from coming to fruition. Paro (28-1, 16 KOs), 30, became a two-division champion when he beat Lewis Crocker by unanimous decision on June 24. The Australian southpaw has won three straight fights since losing his IBF 140-pound title to Richardson Hitchins by split decision in December 2024. “Inside The Ring” streams live every Thursday on DAZN and The Ring’s YouTube channel (2 p.m. ET/7 p.m. BST), providing interviews, analysis and breaking news with the sport's most captivating names.
